title: PEP 541 Request: dst
body:
### Project to be claimed

`PROJECT_NAME`: https://pypi.org/project/dst

### Your PyPI username

`USER_NAME`: https://pypi.org/user/AntonHeikinheimo

### Reasons for the request

Reason (INVALID / abandoned):

Requesting transfer of the abandoned project name dst under PEP 541 ("abandoned" and "the maintainer is unreachable / the project is not functional"). Evidence, all from the PyPI JSON API:

One release ever: 0.0.0a0, uploaded 2023-01-08, nothing since (over three years).
Not a functional project: the only artifacts are a 968-byte wheel and an 808-byte sdist. Empty summary, empty description, no home_page, no project_urls. The version 0.0.0a0 is a placeholder pre-release, never promoted.
No repository or contact is published in the metadata, so the maintainer cannot be reached through the project page.

I maintain dst-core (https://pypi.org/project/dst-core/), the distribution for the open-source "data serve tool (dst)" (https://github.com/get-dst/dst, https://www.dataservetool.com/). The bare dst name is the project's canonical short name and the CLI entry point; the current placeholder squats it with no working software behind it.

What I am asking for: transfer of the dst name so the actively-maintained project can publish under it. I am not asking to remove any working release (there is none beyond the placeholder).

Per PEP 541, PyPI Admins will attempt to contact the current owner and allow a response window before any transfer. I understand this can take time; there is no urgency on my side, dst-core remains our shipping name meanwhile.

### Maintenance or replacement?

None

### Source code repositories URLs

The dst project on PyPI publishes no source repository: its metadata has no home_page, no project_urls, and an empty description, so there is no repository to link.

The project requesting the name:

https://github.com/get-dst — the GitHub organization; the dst repository goes public there at launch (currently staged privately pre-release)
https://pypi.org/project/dst-core/ — our current distribution name
https://www.dataservetool.com/ — documentation site

### Contact and additional research

The package metadata offers no contact channel: no email, no homepage, no repository, no description. Research done:

PyPI user Arwichok (https://pypi.org/user/Arwichok/) — profile exists but lists no contact route.
A GitHub account with the same handle exists and is active (https://github.com/Arwichok, last activity July 2026), but publishes no email; its linked site (arwi.ovh) lists no contact address either.
The dst project itself: a single pre-release 0.0.0a0 (968-byte wheel + 808-byte sdist) uploaded 2023-01-08, with nothing before or since — consistent with a name reservation rather than a functional project.
I have not been able to reach the owner directly through any published channel; I understand PyPI admins will make the formal contact attempt per the PEP 541 process.

title: PEP 541 Request: groundcontrol
body:
### Project to be claimed

`groundcontrol`: https://pypi.org/project/groundcontrol/

### Your PyPI username

`dshean`: https://pypi.org/user/dshean/

### Reasons for the request

The name is held by a project that meets all three PEP 541 abandonment criteria:

- **No releases within the past twelve months.** The only release, `0.1.0.dev0`, was uploaded 2022-07-21 — roughly four years ago.
- **No activity on the project's home page.** No home page or repository is listed; the PyPI project description is empty.
- **Owner reachability.** Two direct, good-faith contact attempts — 2026-08-08 and 2026-08-23, both to the only address in the package metadata — have received no response (both quoted in full below). Confirming reachability is the moderators' step.

The existing release contains essentially no code (verified from the published sdist, 1132 bytes):

- `groundcontrol/__init__.py` is 80 bytes containing only a docstring — no functions, classes, or importable behavior.
- The bundled `README` is the single line `# Ecliptica`, a different project name than the distribution.
- `setup.py` carries commented-out references to another package (`jangada`) plus commented-out `url`, `license`, and `install_requires` — recycled scaffolding rather than a deliberate release.
- The distribution declares no dependencies, no license, and no project URLs.

Download statistics indicate the project is not being used: pypistats (excluding mirrors) shows 98 downloads total over the six months 2026-02-24 to 2026-08-21, and 14 in the last 30 days — scanner-level traffic.

The replacement project already exists and meets notability requirements: https://github.com/uw-cryo/groundcontrol is a publicly released, MIT-licensed scientific Python library for geodetic ground control and DEM accuracy assessment, developed at the University of Washington and archived on Zenodo (concept DOI 10.5281/zenodo.21846300).

A fork under a different name is not an acceptable workaround here. PyPI's own similar-name protection blocks every close variant: `ground-control`, `ground_control`, etc. all ultranormalize identically to the held name, so no separator variant can be registered while the abandoned package exists — the only alternatives are substantively different names that fragment the project's identity across its repository, import name, documentation, and archival DOI, all of which use `groundcontrol`. Meanwhile `pip install groundcontrol` succeeds silently and installs the empty package for anyone who types the natural name of our project (verified in a clean environment); our documentation warns about this at both install call sites because readers otherwise land on the empty package. Reassignment eliminates that hazard; renaming our project does not.

### Maintenance or replacement?

Replacement

### Source code repositories URLs

Replacement project: https://github.com/uw-cryo/groundcontrol
Current holder's project: none linked (no homepage, repository, or project URLs in its metadata).

### Contact and additional research

I have made two direct contact attempts, both to rafaeluz821@gmail.com — the address listed in the package's Author field, and the only contact channel present anywhere in the package's metadata (no repository, homepage, or project URL is listed).

**2026-08-08** — asked whether he would be willing to transfer the name, explicitly offering a no-pressure decline. No response.

**2026-08-23** — followed up, restating the request with the concrete steps and again offering an explicit decline. This message also told him plainly that I intended to file this PEP 541 request if I did not hear back, and that PyPI's admins would contact him directly before anything happened, so he would still have a say. I would rather he hear it from me than be surprised by moderator outreach. No response as of filing.

I will update this issue immediately if he responds, and will withdraw the request if he would prefer to keep the name.

The first email (2026-08-08), verbatim:

```
Hi Rafael,

I've been working on a Python package that automatically fetches high-accuracy 3D ground control points for validating (and perhaps calibrating) 3D terrain models, and ultimately for refining satellite ephemeris and attitude data. It's an open-source academic project at the University of Washington, needed for ongoing NASA projects: https://github.com/uw-cryo/groundcontrol

After months of development I finally made it public and cut an initial release tonight so other users and packages can start integrating - and then realized the PyPI name wasn't available. :(

I see you have a groundcontrol project on PyPI from July 2022. From the sdist it looks like a placeholder - the only module is an __init__.py with just a docstring, and the README says "Ecliptica" - so I'm guessing it isn't going to see further development under the groundcontrol name.

Would you be willing to hand over the PyPI slot? I'd really appreciate it. If you're open to it, the easiest path is to add me as an Owner on the project (Manage -> Collaborators, username dshean - I also maintain some legacy packages on PyPI: pygeotools, demcoreg), and then remove yourself. Happy to walk you through it, or work around whatever's easiest for you.

If you'd rather hold onto it, please let me know. Either way, thanks for considering.

-David
```

The follow-up (2026-08-23), verbatim:

```
Hi Rafael,

Following up on my email from August 8 about the groundcontrol name on PyPI. No worries if you were out or email got buried.

Short version: I maintain an open-source scientific Python library called groundcontrol (https://github.com/uw-cryo/groundcontrol) at the University of Washington, for geodetic ground control and 3D accuracy assessment. I'd like to publish it to PyPI under that name, which your 0.1.0.dev0 release from 2022 currently holds.

If you're willing, it's two steps at https://pypi.org/manage/project/groundcontrol/collaboration/ -- add `dshean` as Owner, then remove yourself. If you'd rather keep the name, just say so and that's the end of it; I'll use a different one and there are no hard feelings.

If I don't hear back, I plan to file a PEP 541 name-transfer request with PyPI. Their admins would contact you directly before anything happened, so you'd still have a say. Just wanted to give you a heads up.

Thanks,
-David
https://github.com/dshean
```

Additional research conducted:

- Downloaded and inspected the sdist (sha256 2916a9c4…); the code-content findings above are measured from the extracted archive.
- Download statistics pulled from pypistats (numbers above).
- Verified `pip install groundcontrol` installs the empty package without error or warning in a clean venv.

I maintain related scientific-geospatial packages on PyPI as `dshean` (account since 2016): pygeotools, demcoreg, imview, vmap.

title: PEP 541 Request: tc420 (https://pypi.org/project/tc420/)
body:
### Project to be claimed

`tc420`: https://pypi.org/project/tc420

### Your PyPI username

`schwabix`: https://pypi.org/user/schwabix

### Reasons for the request

Subject: PEP 541 request — claim inactive/abandoned project tc420

Project name: tc420 (https://pypi.org/project/tc420/)
Current owner: Adam Wallner (wallneradam), adam.wallner@gmail.com
Requester: Markus Kuhn, GitHub: schwabix-1311

Summary:
Requesting transfer of the PyPI project tc420 under PEP 541. The maintainer has been inactive since mid-2021 and unresponsive to all outreach since; the current PyPI release is broken by an unaddressed dependency change.

Evidence of inactivity:
- Last commit to the repo: 2021-07-14 (https://github.com/wallneradam/tc420/commit/b20468e). Last PyPI release: 2021-01-03 (v0.2.1).
- 12 open issues/PRs from 8 different contributors, dated Oct 2021 through June 2024, none acknowledged: https://github.com/wallneradam/tc420/issues and https://github.com/wallneradam/tc420/pulls


My fork: https://github.com/schwabix-1311/tc420 — merges all of the above fixes (click 8.1.0 compat, non-sudo usage, USBTimeoutErrors, multi-controller support) plus the fix for the currently-broken PyPI release. Currently versioned 0.5, ready to publish.

Intent: Publish a fixed, maintained release under the existing name, retaining Adam Wallner's original copyright/attribution per GPLv3+. Open to co-maintainer status instead of full transfer if he resurfaces.

### Maintenance or replacement?

Maintenance

### Source code repositories URLs

current owner's repo: https://github.com/wallneradam/tc420
my forked repo: https://github.com/schwabix-1311/tc420

### Contact and additional research

Evidence of inactivity:
- Last commit to the repo: 2021-07-14 (https://github.com/wallneradam/tc420/commit/b20468e). Last PyPI release: 2021-01-03 (v0.2.1).
- 12 open issues/PRs from 8 different contributors, dated Oct 2021 through June 2024, none acknowledged: https://github.com/wallneradam/tc420/issues and https://github.com/wallneradam/tc420/pulls

Evidence the current release is broken:
- PR #11 (2023-02-26, https://github.com/wallneradam/tc420/pull/11) — fix for click >= 8.1.0 renaming resultcallback to result_callback, submitted and never merged.
- Issue #18 (2024-05-07, https://github.com/wallneradam/tc420/issues/18) — user hitting exactly that breakage: 'Group' object has no attribute 'resultcallback'.

Evidence of direct, unanswered outreach from me:
- PR #12 (2023-03-25, non-sudo usage), PR #13 (2023-03-26, USBTimeoutErrors fix for issue #9), PR #15 / issue #14 (2023-04-19/05-11, multi-controller support) — all open, no maintainer response in 2+ years.
- My comment on issue #9 (2024-07-21, https://github.com/wallneradam/tc420/issues/9#issuecomment-2241738663): "Unfortunately Adam did not accept the PR generated by me. He seems to be completely gone." — publicly documenting the abandonment and pointing users to my fork.
- Unanswered attempt to contact Adam directly via email, dated 2024-09-27, which I can forward on request.
